questions.title: Cloudflare Tunnel is killing the performance of my self-hosted n8n, what am I doing wrong?
questions.basis: labelers agree on category; tie-breaker settled reference doubt
questions.fix: Put Nginx in front of n8n as a reverse proxy (forwarding to port 5678) and point the Cloudflare Tunnel or DNS proxy at Nginx instead of directly at the n8n container.

questions.title: HTTP Request node Returns 401 Unauthorized -Invalid API Key
questions.fix: Configure the HTTP Request node to send the API key in the header name and format that the target API's documentation requires (e.g. Authorization: Bearer <key>, or a custom header with the raw key), using header-based authentication or a Header Auth credential.

questions.title: Choosing the Wrong Execution Plan
questions.fix: Run EXPLAIN ANALYZE to compare estimated and actual row counts, then refresh planner statistics with ANALYZE and add an index that matches the query's filter and sort columns (tenant_id, status, created_at).

questions.title: Branches don't execute asynchrousnously?
questions.fix: Build the three LLM requests as separate items in a Code node and send them through a single HTTP Request node with Options → Batching → Items per Batch set to 3, so the requests go out in parallel instead of sequential branches.

questions.title: PostgreSQL Lock Contention Under High-Concurrency n8n Workloads
questions.fix: Keep PostgreSQL transactions short and limited to database operations, doing external API calls before or after the transaction and processing large datasets in smaller batches to reduce lock contention.

questions.title: About n8n usage permanently
questions.basis: labelers agree on category; tie-breaker settled reference doubt
questions.fix: Stop using the expired n8n Cloud trial and self-host the free Community Edition (e.g., via npm or Docker on your own machine or server), exposing it with a tunnel such as ngrok if external access is needed.

questions.title: Wait in one branch, also stalls another branch
questions.fix: Understand that n8n's branches don't run truly in parallel and that a Wait node only blocks its own branch while the execution stays open until the longest branch finishes, so no change is needed (the behavior is expected).

questions.title: N8n 102 Course Bug for topic: Section 2 - Order Webhook Processor
questions.fix: Expose the local n8n instance (port 5678) through a public HTTPS tunnel such as localtunnel (or ngrok) and use that HTTPS URL as the webhook base URL so the course's HTTPS-only testing page can reach the webhook.

questions.title: N8n LDAP Update Node Bug: undefined/null values cause "argument must be a string (was: object)" error (v2.13.4)
questions.basis: JC: needs a human; two labels agree on the category
questions.fix: Do not pass undefined/null to the LDAP Update node's department attribute; branch the logic before the node (e.g. IF/Switch or separate LDAP nodes per action) so department is only included with a real string value when replacing, and omitted when skipping.

questions.title: Unable to copy and paste nodes - on premises Ubuntu server
questions.fix: Access n8n from a browser secure context (HTTPS via a reverse proxy with SSL, or localhost), or add the n8n URL to Chrome's 'unsafely-treat-insecure-origin-as-secure' flag, so the browser allows clipboard paste.

questions.title: @n8n/scan-community-package failing for cred filename
questions.fix: Run the scanner from the beta tag (npx @n8n/scan-community-package@beta @ambriel-io/n8n-nodes-ambriel) because the tagged release had a bug in the cred-filename-against-convention lint check, and the beta carries the fixed lints.

questions.title: Are there workflow execution time limits?
questions.basis: labelers agree on category; tie-breaker settled reference doubt
questions.fix: Recognize that the old 5-minute Starter execution limit is outdated and that n8n Cloud no longer enforces a short per-workflow timeout, so long-running workflows are allowed, with the current limits described in the Cloud docs.

questions.title: CMD / Powershell-Fenster via Execute Command Node öffnen sich nun sichtbar
questions.basis: JC: needs a human; two labels agree on the category
questions.fix: Roll back n8n to the version installed before the update (npm install -g n8n@<previous-version>), because 2.29.7 introduced a regression that makes the Execute Command shell window visible on Windows.

questions.title: Unable to publish workflow
questions.fix: Re-attach the Zendesk API credential to the Zendesk Trigger node (its credentials object was empty), so that publishing registers the webhook with Zendesk using valid authentication instead of a blank payload that returns 400 Bad Request.

questions.title: Local Ollama AI agent connection issue
questions.basis: labelers agree on category; tie-breaker settled reference doubt
questions.fix: Allow the Ollama port (11434) through the Squid proxy ACLs (e.g. add an ACL permitting CONNECT to port 11434) and make sure the AI node's chat request is routed via the proxy, or keep the Ollama host in NO_PROXY so the LangChain node's fetch bypasses it.

questions.title: Handle out-of-order webhook events
questions.fix: Add a version (or sequence/timestamp) column and make the UPDATE conditional with WHERE id = $1 AND version < $3, setting version = $3, so PostgreSQL atomically rejects older events.

questions.title: "[my instance url] it isn't a valid n8n instance."
questions.fix: Open the n8n editor via localhost (e.g., an SSH tunnel to 127.0.0.1:5678) so the relay URL hostname passes the browser extension's hardcoded allowlist, then start Connect Browser Use from the Assistant's Connections panel.

questions.title: Exactly-once processing failure in paginated
questions.fix: Store the pagination cursor and a lock flag in a database table (not workflow static data), acquire the lock before each run, write records idempotently with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, and advance the cursor only after the page is successfully written.

questions.title: How is it possible for one node not to execute?
questions.fix: Do not reference a node in a parallel branch that may not have run yet; put the Get node upstream in a single path or add a Merge node so all branches finish before the downstream node that uses $('Get node B').all() runs.

questions.title: What are the free hosting or generous free plan hosting for workflow but not render or railway
questions.fix: Host n8n in Docker on an always-on free VM, such as Oracle Cloud's Always Free Ampere ARM instance, with an HTTPS reverse proxy, so the Messenger webhook stays reachable.

questions.title: How to extract json string in text file?
questions.fix: In the Edit Fields (Set) node, change the type of the 'data' field from String to Array so the parsed JSON array is kept as real data instead of being coerced to a string ('[object Object]'), and remove the stray leading '=' before the expression.

questions.title: Airtable node resource locator fails with "No bridge acquired for this context" — Cloud 1.123.69
questions.fix: Upgrade the n8n Cloud workspace from 1.123.69 to a newer version in which the 'No bridge acquired' expression-engine bug is fixed, by changing the version in the Cloud dashboard (Manage > Workspace > Updates & maintenance).

questions.title: N8N Task request timed out after 60 seconds
questions.basis: labelers agree on category; tie-breaker settled reference doubt
questions.fix: Restart the stuck task runner container (not the whole n8n instance), then optionally raise the runner task timeout with N8N_RUNNERS_TASK_TIMEOUT.

questions.title: All Google Related Node Error: dummy.stack.replace is not a function (Self-hosted n8n)
questions.fix: Upgrade n8n from 2.15.0 to a newer release (the accepted answer says 2.17+), where the error-handling bug behind 'dummy.stack.replace is not a function' was reportedly fixed.

questions.title: Form ending multiple files
questions.fix: Instead of returning binary from the Form completion node, use a Code node to read each file's real bytes with await this.helpers.getBinaryDataBuffer(), build base64 data-URI download links in HTML, and show them via the Form node's completion message (respondWith text).

questions.title: Ollama Cloud Connection Tested Successfully but Model List Shows No Results
questions.fix: If using the OpenAI node/credential as an OpenAI-compatible API to reach Ollama Cloud, set the base URL to https://ollama.com/v1 instead of https://ollama.com (the native Ollama nodes work with https://ollama.com).

questions.title: How to upload first file after sorted ascending order?
questions.fix: Split the decompressed binary properties into separate items, sort them by file name, and use a Limit node to keep only the first item before sending it to the HTTP Request node.

questions.title: Unexpected behavior for the "Code" node
questions.fix: Set the Code node's typeVersion to 2 in the workflow JSON sent through the API, because version 1 of the node does not support the Python language option and shows both editors.

questions.title: How to rename the downloaded file?
questions.fix: In the Code node, replace the single-quoted string with a JavaScript template literal (backticks) using item.json.title and item.json.number, and assign it to item.binary.data.fileName before returning the item.

questions.title: N8n Cloud: Send Email (SMTP) node hangs and fails silently — is outbound SMTP (465/587) blocked on Cloud?
questions.fix: Match the SMTP port to the TLS setting in the Send Email node (465 with SSL/TLS on, 587 with it off for STARTTLS) and use an app password, or avoid SMTP by sending through a transactional email provider's HTTPS API (SendGrid, Brevo, Postmark, Resend, Mailgun).

questions.title: Error in my memory nodes
questions.fix: Extract the sender ID into a sessionId field in a Set node before the AI Agent, then set the memory node's Key parameter to {{ $json.sessionId }} so it resolves when the agent runs tools.

questions.title: Asana webhook heartbeats creating thousands of no-op executions — how to suppress storage?
questions.fix: Set the gatekeeper (router) workflow's workflow settings to not save successful production executions, so heartbeat executions are not stored, and forward only real events to a second workflow that saves its executions.

questions.title: Migrating auto-generated encryptionKey from config file to N8N_ENCRYPTION_KEY environment variable resets instance
questions.fix: Stop Docker Compose from mangling the key: put the exact encryptionKey value from the config file directly in the compose file, or single-quote it in `.env` and escape any `$` as `$$`, so N8N_ENCRYPTION_KEY matches the config file's key.

questions.title: No network connection. CloudRun - Help needed
questions.fix: Set the environment variable N8N_ENDPOINT_HEALTH=health on the Cloud Run n8n service so the health endpoint works and the editor stops reporting 'No network connection'.

questions.title: Mailjet Credentials | Sandbox setting gets synced when working with environments
questions.basis: labelers agree on category; tie-breaker settled reference doubt
questions.fix: Treat the synced Mailjet sandbox credential setting as an n8n bug and work around it by keeping sandbox vs live out of the credential, for example by using an HTTP Request node with an environment-variable base URL or separate credentials per environment, and file a GitHub bug.

questions.title: Considerations when deleting user account
questions.fix: In the delete-user dialog, choose to transfer the user's workflows and credentials to another user; tags are instance-wide so they stay on the workflows, and afterwards verify shared credentials and that active/webhook workflows remain activated.

questions.title: Safely handle PostgreSQL transaction failures
questions.fix: Run the UPDATE and INSERT together in a single PostgreSQL transaction (BEGIN ... COMMIT, ROLLBACK on failure), for example in one multi-statement query, so both succeed or fail together.

questions.title: AI Agent tool executes successfully but LLM ignores the returned JSON data (Availability Slots)
questions.basis: JC: the key step is on the page
questions.fix: Stop using agents as tools (the Agent Tool node) for the sub-agent; instead modularize by moving each sub-agent into its own workflow and call it from the orchestrator with the Execute Workflow (sub-workflow) node/tool.

questions.title: Issues with sending report http request to caldav api
questions.fix: Bypass the HTTP Request node, which drops the body for the REPORT method, by making the REPORT request with the XML body, Depth header and auth directly from a Code node using fetch (or the https module).

questions.title: Chat Hub Deprectiation - v3
questions.fix: Replace Chat Hub with a Form Trigger (Authentication set to n8n User Auth) that has a Checkboxes field listing the flows, route each selection to an Execute Sub-workflow node, and end with an n8n Form node (Form Ending, Show Completion Screen) whose completion message reports the sub-workflow results.

questions.title: Cannot get ANY time filters to work
questions.fix: Convert the RSS pubDate string to a numeric timestamp with new Date($json.pubDate).getTime() and compare it with $now.minus({days: 10}).toMillis() using a Number 'Greater than' operator in the Filter node.

questions.title: AI Agent stop when tool fail
questions.basis: labelers agree on category; tie-breaker settled reference doubt
questions.fix: Downgrade the AI Agent node's typeVersion from 3.1 to 2.2 by editing the node JSON, as a workaround for a v3.1 bug where a failing or empty tool result stops the agent.

questions.title: Email addresse
questions.fix: Use a personal email address to sign up, since n8n does not restrict sign-up to company emails (only some external services may require a corporate email).

questions.title: Configuring n8n to use Open WebUI's Ollama instance
questions.fix: Set the Ollama credential's Base URL to the Open WebUI Ollama proxy path (https://yourdomain/ollama, with no trailing slash) so that /api/tags reaches Open WebUI's Ollama API proxy instead of its web UI.

questions.title: Code search tools
questions.fix: Give the AI agent HTTP Request Tool nodes that call GitHub's code search API (https://api.github.com/search/code) with a repo-scoped q parameter filled via $fromAI, authenticated with GitHub credentials, so the agent can search the codebase.

questions.title: N8n self hosted on OVH : tips and tricks?
questions.basis: labelers agree on category; tie-breaker settled reference doubt
questions.fix: Move n8n off the OVH preinstalled package to a self-managed Docker Compose setup, update by pulling the newer n8n image and recreating the container, and set core environment variables (N8N_HOST, N8N_PROTOCOL, WEBHOOK_URL, GENERIC_TIMEZONE, N8N_ENCRYPTION_KEY, database settings) in the compose file.

questions.title: Create a JSON object as input for Loop over Items node
questions.basis: JC: the key step is on the page
questions.fix: Generate 5 separate items (e.g., with a Code node that returns an array of {json: {...}} objects) before the Loop Over Items node, because the loop iterates over items, not over an array inside a single item.

questions.title: Issue with an error on an AI agent I don't get and CGPT neither
questions.fix: Set the AI Agent node's 'Source for Prompt (User Message)' dropdown to 'Define below' (it only accepts its two preset options, not custom text or an expression), then put the message.content expression in the Prompt (User Message) field.

questions.title: Email attachments not sending via SMTP node in n8n 2.3.0 (self-hosted)
questions.fix: Re-attach the IMAP trigger's binary data to the item just before the Send email node (e.g. with a Code node returning json plus binary from the trigger), then set the Attachments option to the binary property names on that item, e.g. {{ Object.keys($binary).join(',') }}.

questions.title: N8N on intranet
questions.basis: JC: the key step is on the page
questions.fix: Confirm that no reverse proxy is needed and set WEBHOOK_URL and N8N_EDITOR_BASE_URL to the internal domain/IP with port 5678 (http), as already configured, so the setup works on the internal network.

questions.title: How to create a new sheet in a Google Sheet document with the same columns as the existing sheet in it?
questions.basis: JC: the key step is on the page
questions.fix: Stop relying on the AI agent to invent column names: read the 'shares' sheet headers deterministically (e.g. Google Sheets Get Rows plus a Code node), create the new sheet, then write the same column headers and rows to it with explicitly defined column mapping in regular (non-tool) nodes.

questions.title: N8n and automation testing
questions.fix: Start n8n with a fixed N8N_ENCRYPTION_KEY, call POST /rest/owner/setup once to create the owner, then call POST /rest/me/api-keys to mint an API key, and snapshot and reuse the Postgres volume across CI runs.

questions.title: Basic LLM Chain - Model output doesn't fit required format
questions.basis: JC: the key step is on the page
questions.fix: Replace the Basic LLM Chain with an AI Agent node that has a strict prompt on output format and a connected Structured Output Parser, optionally adding the Auto-fixing Output Parser so a second LLM call repairs malformed output.

questions.title: How to activate my n8n creator page after registering as a creator?
questions.fix: Submit workflow templates to the n8n template library and get them approved (reportedly around 3), after which the creator page goes live automatically.

questions.title: Way to Handle Long-Running AI Workflows in n8n Without Execution Timeouts
questions.fix: Respond to the webhook immediately and run the long processing asynchronously, splitting it into separate stages (e.g. sub-workflows or a queue/worker) that save checkpoints and retry only the failed stage.

questions.title: Prevent n8n workflows from processing the same job twice after a worker failure
questions.fix: Claim jobs atomically in PostgreSQL with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED inside an UPDATE, and guard every later update with a lease timeout and a worker_id condition (WHERE id = $1 AND status = 'processing' AND worker_id = $2) so stale workers cannot overwrite reclaimed jobs.

questions.title: Prevent a single bad item from corrupting long-running n8n executions
questions.fix: Catch errors per item inside the Code/Function node and return them as data with a status field, then route failed items to a dead-letter table, and make DB writes idempotent with UPSERT so retries don't create duplicates.

questions.title: The easiest way to handle chatbot messages
questions.basis: JC: the key step is on the page
questions.fix: Store each incoming message in an n8n Data Table with a 'pending' status, wait x seconds, then check whether it is still the latest message; if so, combine all pending messages into one for processing and mark them 'Processed', otherwise do nothing.

questions.title: How do you verify AI workflows actually did the right thing?
questions.fix: Add human-in-the-loop review, with manual output checks during build and a periodic human review every x runs, to verify AI workflow results after execution.

questions.title: Alterar campo de credenciais llm dinamicamente via Expressions não está funcionando
questions.basis: JC: the key step is on the page
questions.fix: In the OpenAI credential's API key field, enable Expression mode and enter {{ $json.apiKey }} (ignoring the 'no path back to the node' warning), and set the model name manually as a fixed or expression value because the model list can't be fetched.

questions.title: Handling strict hourly API fetches and retries: Using n8n as a middleware cache
questions.basis: JC: the key step is on the page
questions.fix: Use the Schedule Trigger workflow to store the fetched result in n8n Variables or workflow static data, and add a separate GET Webhook workflow that reads that store and returns the cached value with a Respond to Webhook node (retries come from the HTTP Request node's Retry On Fail settings, with Wait Between Tries, or from a custom loop).

questions.title: Shopify trigger error
questions.fix: Delete the copy-pasted Shopify Trigger node and add a fresh Shopify Trigger node (not pasted) in each workflow, so each gets its own unique webhook path/ID and the activation conflict clears; use a separate trigger per topic (create/update/delete).

questions.title: Webhook Test Mode 500 – Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'name') (Cloud 2.6.3)
questions.fix: Open the Webhook node and fix its Respond setting: either add and connect a Respond to Webhook node, or change 'Respond' to 'Immediately' or 'When Last Node Finishes' so the test-mode response-mode check no longer hits a missing child node.

questions.title: Supabase vector store for AI agent retrieval
questions.fix: Create a match_documents SQL function in Supabase with the signature (query_embedding vector(1536), match_count int, filter jsonb) that queries the knowledge_chunks table, replacing the old match_threshold version, and reload the PostgREST schema cache.

questions.title: N8n Workflow Fails to Resume Safely After Partial Execution (Idempotency & Checkpointing Issue)
questions.fix: Persist the last successfully processed page number in an external database, read it at the start of each run to resume from the next page, and update it only after that page has been processed and stored.

questions.title: How to filter files under 5GB in size from RSS?
questions.fix: Use a Code node to parse the size string (number plus MiB/GiB unit) from the RSS item with a regular expression, convert everything to a common unit (GiB), and return only items where the size is under 5.

questions.title: How do agencies handle client onboarding
questions.basis: JC: the key step is on the page
questions.fix: After importing the exported workflow JSON into the client's instance, the client must create their own credentials (credentials are not included in the export) and manually re-link them to each node, and update environment-specific values such as IDs and webhook URLs.

questions.title: HTTPRequest sending single variable as JSON
questions.fix: Send the body as a JSON object with a key wrapping the variable (e.g. {"intent": "{{ $json.cleanOutput }}"}) instead of sending the raw variable alone, using the key name the target API expects.

questions.title: N8n trial about ends soon— Docker desktop appraoch
questions.fix: Install Podman on Windows via winget, initialize and start a Podman machine (WSL 2/Hyper-V VM), then run `podman compose up -d` in the n8n directory to self-host n8n as an alternative to Docker Desktop.

questions.title: Allow additional functions/modules in Task-Runners is not possible by env variables
questions.fix: Mount a custom n8n-task-runners.json into the task runner container at /etc/n8n-task-runners.json that sets the allowed builtin/external modules (NODE_FUNCTION_ALLOW_BUILTIN / NODE_FUNCTION_ALLOW_EXTERNAL) in env-overrides or adds them to allowed-env.

questions.title: Master workflow does not trigger when the error occurs at the sub-workflow level
questions.basis: JC: the key step is on the page
questions.fix: Set the Error Workflow in the sub-workflow's own settings (or route the Execute Sub-workflow node's error output to the error reporter), because an error workflow set on the master only fires when the master execution itself fails, and manual runs do not trigger error workflows.

questions.title: Can't process a matrix of hosts in n8n
questions.basis: JC: the key step is on the page
questions.fix: Wire the triggers (Manual Trigger and Schedule Trigger) into the Code node, and connect the Code node's output to Execute Command, so the Code node's 8 items flow through Execute Command, which runs once per item. Previously the triggers fed Execute Command directly, so it received only one item.

questions.title: Executive Sub-workflow node
questions.fix: Convert the comma-separated string passed into the sub-workflow's fieldsList input into a real array (e.g. with an expression like {{$json.fieldsList.split(',')}}) so the value matches the array input type.

questions.title: The badge :)
questions.fix: An n8n staff member with admin access to the course platform must assign the missing Level 1 course badge to the user's account, after cleaning up duplicate accounts.

questions.title: Instance-level MCP settings not persisting via UI (self-hosted Docker)
questions.fix: Upgrade n8n from 2.8.3 to version 2.9.0 or later, which includes the fix for the MCP toggle in workflow settings not persisting (PR #25630).

questions.title: Multiple Attachments Mail via outlook
questions.fix: Rename each item's binary field to a unique name (e.g. data1, data2) with a Set/Edit Fields node, merge the items into a single item, then list each binary property name as an attachment in one Outlook node so only one email is sent.

questions.title: Workspace offline (503) – Urgent - memory limit hit during first test?
questions.fix: Turn off downloadAttachments on the Gmail trigger so it returns only metadata, then fetch each PDF one at a time with a Gmail 'Get a Message Attachment' node inside a SplitInBatches loop (batch size 1) so only one attachment is held in memory.

questions.title: Safely process large datasets
questions.basis: labelers agree on category; tie-breaker settled reference doubt
questions.fix: Paginate at the API (fetch a page at a time), process each page in batches with Loop Over Items (Split in Batches), and offload heavy processing to sub-workflows so the full dataset is never held in one execution's memory.

questions.title: Cloud Instance 503 Loop - Down for 12+ Hours
questions.fix: n8n staff/engineering must repair the crashing Cloud workspace backend (e.g., failed migration or database problem), which the customer cannot do themselves; the customer should keep the support ticket open and provide workspace ID and the time the loop started.

questions.title: Is there a way to put description in the workflow with the n8n API
questions.fix: Send a PUT request to /api/v1/workflows/{id} with a top-level 'description' field in the body (not inside meta), alongside name, nodes, connections, and a cleaned settings object that contains only accepted fields such as executionOrder.

questions.title: Workflow stuck executing "old" Airtable record
questions.basis: JC: the key step is on the page
questions.fix: Inspect the AI Agent's actual input in a recent execution and check for stale data upstream: the Airtable filter returning completed records, the Split In Batches loop reusing an old item, expressions using $items()/.first()/another node's output, and any connected memory on the AI Agent. Fix whichever of these supplies the old topic.

questions.title: N8n Cloud – Workspace offline (503) when scheduled workflow runs
questions.fix: Add pruning logic at the start of the Deduplication Code node so the seenPlaceIds and seenEmails arrays in $getWorkflowStaticData('node') are capped (e.g. keep only the last ~5000 entries) or reset, so they stop growing and exhausting workspace memory.

questions.title: Cost of using Chatgpt(Tokens)
questions.fix: Reduce the tokens sent per run by lowering the vector store retrieval Top K (about 3-5), shrinking the memory context window (or disabling memory), and merging the input into a single field so the model runs once.

questions.title: Workflow executes but says error on last step (it works)
questions.fix: Remove the extra incoming connection (likely the direct one from the AI node) to the HTTP Request node, so it runs only once with the correct input data that includes media[0].source_url.

questions.title: N8n API Pagination returns the same cursor
questions.basis: JC: the key step is on the page
questions.fix: Configure the HTTP Request node's built-in pagination to send a 'cursor' query parameter set to {{ $response.body.nextCursor }} (or use the built-in n8n API node, which handles pagination), instead of manually reusing the cursor.

questions.title: Invalid URL error on Discord node
questions.basis: labelers agree on category; tie-breaker settled reference doubt
questions.fix: Replace the Discord node's webhook send with an HTTP Request node that POSTs to the Discord webhook URL, since the Discord node's webhook path has a bug (tracked as NODE-5739) that no setting fixes.

questions.title: 100 nodes with issues after workflow clone
questions.basis: JC: the key step is on the page
questions.fix: Instead of cloning/duplicating the workflow, export the workflow to JSON and import it into a new workflow (or copy all nodes and paste them into a new workflow), which keeps the Supabase node parameters like the table from needing a refresh.

questions.title: How to have 2 facebook Lead ad trigger nodes in n8n
questions.basis: labelers agree on category; tie-breaker settled reference doubt
questions.fix: Configure both Facebook Lead Ads Trigger nodes (one per form) with credentials from the same Facebook app, because separate apps do not both deliver webhook events to n8n.

questions.title: Need your help
questions.fix: Open the community profile preferences (Discourse user settings) and uncheck the option that hides the profile and presence from public view, so the profile page is publicly accessible.

questions.title: Google Sheets Trigger returning intermittent 503 Service Unavailable across multiple workflows over 24+ hours
questions.basis: JC: the key step is on the page
questions.fix: Switch the Google Sheets Trigger from n8n's shared OAuth client to a custom OAuth client (own Google Cloud OAuth credentials) to isolate from shared-client failures, and use a push/webhook trigger with a scheduled reconciliation sweep for reliability.

questions.title: Update: Ruled out ngrok interstitial + proxy headers, still no executions
questions.fix: Use the Meta Graph API Explorer to POST to <WABA_ID>/subscribed_apps so the customer's own app is subscribed to the WhatsApp Business Account, then verify with GET and republish the workflow.

questions.title: I'm using an AI Agent with three different tools: HTTP Request Code Vector Store
questions.fix: Rewrite each tool's description to be explicit and non-overlapping (e.g. tell the HTTP Request tool to be used only when live API data is required, and the vector store tool for stored knowledge) so the agent's model picks the correct tool.

questions.title: Updading the Gmail node to the latest version
questions.basis: JC: the key step is on the page
questions.fix: Enable Retry On Fail on the Gmail node (and reduce request bursts), since the intermittent 500 backendError comes from Google's side rather than from the node version 2.1 vs 2.2; optionally replace the node with a fresh one to compare.

questions.title: Way to Handle Workflow Version Drift Across Multiple
questions.fix: Drain the workers before deploying: stop new jobs from entering the queue, let running executions finish, deploy the new workflow version, then resume processing.

questions.title: Entra ID integration query?
questions.basis: labelers agree on category; tie-breaker settled reference doubt
questions.fix: Use the HTTP Request node (or the built-in Slack node) to call each app's own API, such as Slack's SCIM API for account creation and disabling and Plausible's guests invite endpoint, to automate provisioning from n8n workflows. This is provisioning only, not SSO.

questions.title: What Airtable alternatives do people actually use
questions.fix: Use Supabase (table editor) as the Airtable replacement for structured data with n8n handling automations, or choose NocoDB/Baserow if the team is non-technical and needs a spreadsheet-like UI.

questions.title: WhatsApp Trigger webhook won't validate — generic "Invalid parameter" / callback verification fails, self-hosted Docker + ngrok
questions.basis: labelers agree on category; tie-breaker settled reference doubt
questions.fix: Set the WEBHOOK_URL environment variable (the answer writes it as N8N_WEBHOOK_URL) to the full public https ngrok URL with a trailing slash and restart the container, so n8n gives Meta an HTTPS callback URL instead of http://localhost:5678.

306585.text:
I’m sorry, but the provided n8n documentation excerpts don’t cover PostgreSQL query planner behavior or how to judge whether a query plan is “poor.” They do mention that n8n databases can grow with execution volume and that saving/pruning execution data can help improve database performance [1][2][4].

What you’re seeing is expected behavior in n8n.

In workflows created from n8n 1.0, branches run **one after another**, not simultaneously: n8n completes one branch before starting the next, ordered by their position on the canvas [4]. So if one branch contains a Wait node, the other branch won’t start until that branch finishes waiting.

The Wait node pauses the workflow execution and resumes it later with the same data [1][2]. For short waits under 65 seconds, n8n does **not** offload the execution data to the database; the process keeps running until the interval passes [6]. That can make the workflow appear to stall.

If you need truly independent parallel execution, this is not covered by the docs I have here. Please contact n8n support or ask in the n8n community forum.

Your error is likely because `inputDataFieldName` expects a **single binary field name**, but your code sets it to a comma-separated list from `Object.keys($binary).join(',')`, which produces `data1,data2` [1]. That won’t match an actual binary field name, so n8n reports: **“No binary data with field data1,data2 found.”**

What you can do:
- Return **one file** from the Form Ending by setting **Input Data Field Name** to a single binary property name [1].
- If you need multiple downloaded files, the docs here don’t cover a supported way to return multiple binaries from a single form completion [1]. You may need to combine them into one file, or handle downloads another way.
- For binary data handling, n8n supports working with files through nodes like **Convert to File**, **Extract From File**, and **Read/Write Files from Disk** [2].

If you’d like, I recommend contacting **n8n support** or asking in the **n8n community forum** for the best pattern for returning multiple modified files from a form [1][2].

Your Code node is already picking the first file after sorting, but the **HTTP Request** node is still hardcoded to upload `file_0`:

```json
"inputDataFieldName": "file_0"
```

So even if `Code1` returns a different binary key, the next node still looks for `file_0`.

### Fix
Change **inputDataFieldName** in the HTTP Request node to the same binary key you output from the Code node, or make it dynamic.

For example, in your Code node you return:

```js
return [{
  json: {},
  binary: {
    [firstKey]: firstFile
  }
}];
```

Then in the HTTP Request node, use the binary property name that matches that returned key instead of always `file_0`.

### Why
n8n’s workflow behavior depends on node data and configuration; the docs here explain workflow execution and data handling, but they don’t cover this specific upload setup in detail [2][4]. If you want, I can help you rewrite the Code and HTTP Request nodes so the upload always uses the first sorted file.

If you still run into trouble, please contact n8n support or ask in the n8n community forum [1].

You can rename the **binary file name** by setting the `fileName` property on the binary data, not by using the Set node field name. n8n uses the binary data’s file name for later upload operations like SSH Upload File, and you can override it with the **File Name** option if needed [4].

In a Code node, update the binary property directly, for example:

```javascript
for (const item of $input.all()) {
  item.binary.data.fileName = `${item.json.title}_${item.json.number}.zip`;
}
return $input.all();
```

In your current workflow, this line won’t interpolate the variables correctly because it’s wrapped in single quotes:

```javascript
'${json.title}_{json.number}.zip'
```

Use backticks and reference the item’s JSON data instead. Also, make sure you’re setting the file name on the binary data itself, since the HTTP Request node and other upload nodes rely on the binary file name [1][4].

If you’re uploading to another service and it expects a specific file name, set that on the binary before the upload node, or use the node’s **File Name** option where available [1][4].

If you want, I can help rewrite your full workflow so the merge/code step produces the exact filename you need.

It sounds like your **memory node is getting a session key from a value that’s not available in the tool-execution path**.

A few relevant points from the docs:

- **Simple Memory** uses a **Session Key** field to store memory, and it keeps a set number of previous interactions via **Context Window Length** [1].
- For **Postgres Chat Memory**, if you use multiple memory nodes, they share the same memory instance unless you set different **session IDs** [3].
- In n8n, **memory works with AI agent nodes**, but **AI chains can’t use memory** [1][4].

### Why this may happen
Since your workflow is triggered by a **webhook** and not a **Chat Trigger**, you are not using the `Connected Chat Trigger Node` session flow. If the key is coming from data that is only present in the normal message path, it may be **undefined when the agent calls a tool**, which causes the “Key parameter is empty” error.

### What to try
- Make sure the **Key / Session Key** is set to a value that is always present for every execution, including when tools are used.
- If you’re using a webhook, use a stable ID from the webhook payload or generate one before the agent runs.
- Avoid relying on values that may only exist in part of the workflow execution, such as fields produced later in the flow.

### If it still fails
The docs here don’t cover this exact webhook + tool-calling memory issue. I’d recommend contacting **n8n support** or asking in the **n8n community forum**.

Yes — in n8n, input data between nodes must be an **array of objects**, and each item should usually be wrapped in a `json` key [6].

If you want the Loop Over Items node to run 5 times, create **5 items** like this in your Set node:

```json
[
  { "json": { "value": 1 } },
  { "json": { "value": 2 } },
  { "json": { "value": 3 } },
  { "json": { "value": 4 } },
  { "json": { "value": 5 } }
]
```

The Loop Over Items node then processes the items in batches, and if you want it to process one item at a time, set **Batch Size** to `1` [4]. The node stores the original incoming data and returns each batch through the **loop** output, then combines everything and returns it through **done** [1].

If you’re using the Set node, make sure you’re creating **multiple items**, not one object containing multiple objects. The syntax you pasted is not valid JSON as written because it’s missing the outer array and `json` wrapping [6].

A simple example of 5 items would be:

```json
[
  { "json": { "color": "red", "value": "#f00" } },
  { "json": { "color": "green", "value": "#0f0" } },
  { "json": { "color": "blue", "value": "#00f" } },
  { "json": { "color": "cyan", "value": "#0ff" } },
  { "json": { "color": "magenta", "value": "#f0f" } }
]
```

If you want, I can also show you how to build this directly in the Set node UI.

The reply correctly says 5 items are needed, but tells the customer to put the array with `json` wrappers into the Set node. That would still produce a single item, so the loop would run once and the customer would be back. The reply never suggests the Code node.

A single Set node field would still produce one item, with the `json` wrapper as literal data, so the loop would still run once. The `json`-key wrapping only applies to Code node output. The reference's fix is a Code node that returns 5 items, and the reply never mentions it.

The reply incorrectly tells the user to define an array of 5 items inside the Set node, which is impossible because the Set node outputs 1 item per incoming item and cannot expand an array into separate items. Following this advice will leave the user with a single item, causing the loop to execute only once.

For long-running workflows, n8n recommends a few patterns that fit your use case:

- **Use queue mode/background workers** so production executions are processed by worker processes. This helps move heavy work off the main process, though it can add some overhead for webhooks [1].
- **Return immediately from the webhook and continue asynchronously**. On n8n Cloud, webhooks must respond within **100 seconds** or the request fails with a **524** error. The docs suggest using **two webhooks**: one to start the long-running process and send an immediate response, and another to poll for status/result later [2].
- **Split large workflows into smaller parts / sub-workflows** to reduce memory use. n8n recommends processing data in smaller chunks and using sub-workflows that return only a small result set to the parent workflow [3][5].
- **Use the Wait node** if you need to pause and resume later, for example for rate limiting or waiting on an external event [4].

On your specific questions:

- **Best architecture for long-running jobs?** Usually: webhook starts job → workflow writes state/result somewhere → worker/sub-workflows process in batches → client polls or gets notified later [1][2][3][5].
- **How to avoid timeouts and full reprocessing?** Respond quickly to the webhook, store intermediate state outside the running execution, and break the work into smaller batches/sub-workflows so failures don’t restart everything [2][3][5].
- **Split by stage or one large workflow?** The docs lean toward **breaking workflows into smaller parts/sub-workflows** for memory efficiency and better control [3][5].

If you’d like, I can also help outline a n8n-specific workflow structure for this pattern.

For this kind of item-level validation problem, n8n recommends throwing a `NodeOperationError` rather than a plain `Error`. `NodeOperationError` is intended for operational issues like validation failures, missing parameters, data transformation errors, and workflow logic errors [1].

If you’re processing multiple items, include the `itemIndex` when throwing the error so n8n can link it to the specific item [1]. Example:

```ts
throw new NodeOperationError(this.getNode(), "Invalid email address", {
	description: `The email address '${email}' in the 'email' field isn't valid`,
	itemIndex,
});
```

For long-running item processing, n8n also supports looping/batching with the **Loop Over Items** node. Set **Batch Size** to `1` to process items individually, or batch them to reduce the impact of failures and API limits [6]. For nodes that don’t automatically iterate over all items, you may need to design the loop yourself [6].

If you need a workflow to fail intentionally under certain conditions, you can also use the **Stop And Error** node [3].

That said, the docs here don’t cover a full pattern for transactional retries, deduplication, or preventing partial database writes from corrupting retries. For that, I’d suggest contacting n8n support or asking in the n8n community forum.

Yes — for large datasets, n8n recommends reducing memory use by processing data in smaller chunks and splitting workflows into sub-workflows that return only a limited amount of data [2][5]. This is especially important because large JSON/binary payloads, many nodes, and manual executions can increase memory consumption [5].

A good approach here is:

- **Batch the data**: process smaller chunks instead of all records at once, e.g. 200 rows at a time rather than 10,000 [2][5].
- **Use sub-workflows**: let the sub-workflow do the heavy lifting for each batch, then return only a small result set to the parent workflow. This helps free memory after each batch [1][2].
- **Avoid the Code node where possible**: it can increase memory usage significantly [2][5].
- **Don’t save unnecessary execution data**: especially once the workflow is past testing, consider not saving successful executions [1][3].
- **Avoid manual executions for large datasets**: they use extra memory because n8n copies data for the frontend [2][5].

About your example:

```js
const batchSize = 100;
return $input.all().slice(0, batchSize);
```

That only takes the first 100 items from the current input; by itself it does not create a full batching strategy. The docs recommend using batching/splitting items into smaller chunks and, for larger workflows, combining that with sub-workflows and limited return data [2][5].

The docs you shared don’t specifically cover **streaming** as a recommendation here. If you want guidance on the best design for your exact workflow, I’d suggest contacting n8n support or asking in the n8n community forum.

You’re seeing n8n’s branch execution order, not an LLM-specific issue: in n8n 1.0+ branches run one after another, not at the same time [2].

1. Check your workflow version/order:
   - For workflows created from n8n 1.0, n8n completes one branch before starting the next [2].
   - The branch order is determined by canvas position: topmost first, then leftmost if tied [2].

2. Don’t expect `Merge` to make branches parallel:
   - `Merge` “always waits until the data from both inputs is available” [3].
   - So it can combine results, but it won’t start branches concurrently.

3. If you need the total time to feel shorter:
   - Move the branches into separate workflows and call them separately, or
   - Use a pattern where each LLM call happens in its own workflow and you collect the results afterward.
   - That part is general workflow design knowledge; n8n’s branch execution itself is sequential [2].

4. If you want to confirm what’s happening:

You’re trying to prevent an older webhook from overwriting a newer state, which is best handled in PostgreSQL with a monotonic guard.

1. **Add a versioning field to your table**
   Use one of these, in order of preference:
   - `event_version BIGINT` if the source gives a reliable sequence/version
   - `event_timestamp TIMESTAMPTZ` if the source gives a trustworthy event time
   - both, if you want a tie-breaker

2. **Only update when the incoming event is newer**
   General PostgreSQL approach:
   ```sql
   UPDATE orders
   SET
     status = $2,
     event_version = $3,
     updated_at = NOW()
   WHERE id = $1
     AND (event_version IS NULL OR event_version < $3);
   ```
   If you use timestamps:
   ```sql
   UPDATE orders
   SET
     status = $2,
     event_timestamp = $3,
     updated_at = NOW()
   WHERE id = $1
     AND (event_timestamp IS NULL OR event_timestamp < $3);
   ```

3. **Make it atomic**
   Run the check and update in the same SQL statement like above. That avoids a race where two webhook executions read the same old row and both try to write.

4. **If you need retries to be idempotent**
   Keep a separate table of processed event IDs and reject duplicates before updating:
   ```sql
   INSERT INTO processed_events (event_id, order_id)
   VALUES ($1, $2)
   ON CONFLICT (event_id) DO NOTHING;
   ```
   Then only update `orders` if the insert succeeded.

5. **If events can arrive out of order but not all sources are trustworthy**
   Prefer a source-provided sequence/version over your own timestamp. Server receive time is usually not safe for ordering because network delays can reorder arrivals.

If you want, I can turn this into a single `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE` pattern for PostgreSQL that handles both inserts and updates safely.

The issue is that your two SQL statements are separate operations, so a failure after the first one can leave the database half-updated.

1. **Use a single PostgreSQL transaction for the whole unit of work**. That’s general PostgreSQL behavior, not specific to n8n.
2. **Prefer one SQL script/query that does both writes inside `BEGIN … COMMIT`** if your node/setup supports it. If anything fails, PostgreSQL can `ROLLBACK` the whole transaction.
3. **Keep the workflow idempotent where you can**:
   - `UPDATE customers ... WHERE id = $1`
   - `INSERT INTO customer_logs ...`
   - Make the log insert safe to retry (for example with a unique key on `(customer_id, action, created_at_bucket)` or another business key) so reruns don’t duplicate rows.
4. In n8n, use the **PostgreSQL** node for the SQL and pass customer values as **query parameters** rather than string interpolation, as shown for SQL nodes in the docs [3]. That helps keep the query safe.
5. If your workflow has multiple items, n8n usually processes items automatically one by one [1]. That doesn’t replace database transactions, so don’t rely on workflow order alone to guarantee consistency.

A practical pattern is:
- **PostgreSQL node 1**: start a transaction / run the combined SQL
- **PostgreSQL node 2**: commit only after all statements succeed
- On any error, let PostgreSQL roll back the transaction

If your current n8n PostgreSQL node setup doesn’t expose transaction control directly, the safest approach is to wrap both statements in one database-side transaction-capable query or stored procedure, then call that once from n8n.

grades.why: The reply gets the core answer right: use a PostgreSQL transaction, with idempotency as a complement. It then suggests a two-node BEGIN/COMMIT pattern that would not work reliably in n8n, and it never mentions the Postgres node's Transaction batching option. It does hedge with a single-query or stored-procedure fallback, but the customer could still follow the broken pattern.
grades.error: The 'practical pattern' puts transaction start in one PostgreSQL node and the commit in a second node. n8n does not guarantee the same database session across separate node executions, so BEGIN and COMMIT in different nodes will not reliably form one transaction. The reply also misses the Postgres node's built-in Query Batching 'Transaction' option, which is the n8n-native way to do this.

It also addresses idempotency and provides concrete advice for structuring the query in n8n. The guidance matches the accepted community answer and standard SQL practices.

grades.error: Recommends splitting BEGIN/COMMIT across two PostgreSQL nodes (start in node 1, commit in node 2), which will not share the same DB session and risks leaving an open transaction, instead of the reference fix of one atomic transaction via Query Batching = Transaction.

The likely issue is that the agent is receiving the tool result, but the JSON is too complex or too broad for the model to use reliably, so it answers from its own guess instead of the returned slots.

1. **Reduce the tool payload before it reaches the agent**  
   If `get_availability` is built with an **HTTP Request** tool, turn on **Optimize Response** and return only the fields the agent needs, rather than the full JSON [3].  
   - In the HTTP Request node, enable **Optimize Response**  
   - Choose **JSON**  
   - Set **Field Containing Data** to `data`  
   - Use **Include Fields → Selected** and keep only fields like `start` and `seatsRemaining` [3]

2. **Flatten the shape if possible**  
   Instead of returning:
   ```json
   { "data": { "2026-01-19": [ ... ] } }
   ```
   return something closer to:
   ```json
   { "slots": [ ... ], "date": "2026-01-19" }
   ```
   This is general JSON/API design advice, but it helps LLMs a lot when tool outputs are simple and direct.

3. **Make the agent instruction specific**  
   In the **Instructions** field for the Scheduling Agent, tell it exactly how to use the tool result, for example:  
   - “Always answer only from the `get_availability` tool result.”  
   - “If `data` contains any date keys with slot arrays, list those slots exactly as returned.”  
   - “Do not invent times. If no slots are present, say no availability is shown.”  
   n8n recommends keeping instructions specific and refining them first [6].

4. **If this is a nested tool chain, pass only the relevant context**  
   n8n notes that agents do not pass full execution context by default, so include any needed context in the prompt [1]. If the Scheduling Agent depends on upstream data, make sure the exact date/range is included in its prompt.

If you want, I can help you rewrite the `get_availability` response shape and the Scheduling Agent instructions so the model has a much easier time using the slots correctly.

You’re filtering on an RSS date string, but the Filter node needs a real date/time comparison, not a plain text string comparison.  

1. In the **Filter** node, change the condition to **Date & Time → is after** instead of **equals**. That’s the right comparison for “last 10 days” [7].
2. Set the **left value** to your RSS date field, but convert it if needed. If `pubDate` is a non-standard string, parse it with Luxon using `fromFormat()` [6]. Example:
   ```js
   {{ DateTime.fromFormat($json.pubDate, "EEE, dd LLL yyyy HH:mm:ss ZZZ").toISO() }}
   ```
   If your feed uses a different date format, the format string must match exactly [6].
3. Set the **right value** to:
   ```js
   {{ $today.minus({ days: 10 }) }}
   ```
   or, if you prefer ISO output:
   ```js
   {{ $today.minus({ days: 10 }).toISO() }}
   ```
   (`$today` is the documented n8n date helper [6].)
4. Use the Filter node’s **Date & Time** comparison, not **Is equal / Is not equal**, because those won’t give you “recent than 10 days” logic [7].

Your model output is structurally different from the schema the parser is expecting.

1. Make the model return the fields at the top level, not nested under `output`.
   - Current output:
     ```json
     {"output":{"nsfw":true,"jailbreak":false,"help":false,"substantive":true}}
     ```
   - Expected by the parser:
     ```json
     {"nsfw":true,"jailbreak":false,"help":false,"substantive":true}
     ```

2. Update your Basic LLM Chain prompt so it explicitly forbids wrappers like `output`.
   - In **Basic LLM Chain1 → Prompt (User Message)**, change the instruction to something like:
     ```text
     Return ONLY valid JSON with these top-level keys:
     nsfw, jailbreak, help, substantive

     Do not wrap the result in an "output" object.
     ```
   - The Basic LLM Chain supports a required output parser when **Require Specific Output Format** is enabled [1].

3. Keep the **Structured Output Parser** schema aligned to the top-level fields.
   - Use:
     ```json
     {
       "nsfw": false,
       "jailbreak": true,
       "help": false,
       "substantive": false
     }
     ```
   - The parser is meant to return fields based on a JSON Schema/example, and your example currently defines those fields at the top level [5].

4. If you are using the parsed result in another AI step, remember the docs say the Structured Output Parser is for final output from AI agents, and for intermediary structured data n8n recommends a separate LLM chain rather than parsing directly inside the agent flow [2].

If you want, I can help rewrite your exact prompt so it matches the parser schema cleanly.

You’re hitting three separate limits at once: webhook timeout, memory growth, and long executions being too “all-or-nothing.” The best pattern is to make the webhook respond fast, then do the heavy work in queue mode and smaller stages.

1. **Put the heavy work behind queue mode**  
   In queue mode, the webhook request is handled by the main/webhook process, and the actual execution runs on workers [1][7]. That’s the right fit for long AI jobs.

2. **Return from the webhook immediately**  
   On n8n Cloud, webhooks time out after 100 seconds [5]. Use a short first workflow:
   - `Webhook` → create a job record / enqueue work
   - `Respond to Webhook` immediately with a job ID or “accepted”
   Then have a second workflow poll or continue processing async [5].  
   This is general HTTP design, not just n8n.

3. **Split the workflow into stages**  
   Break `Webhook → Download File → Extract Text → AI Processing → Save Result` into smaller workflows. n8n recommends splitting data into smaller chunks and using sub-workflows with `Execute Workflow` [6]. This reduces memory pressure and makes retries smaller.

4. **Process large documents in batches**  
   Use `Loop Over Items` / `Split In Batches` to chunk the document before AI calls [2][6]. Each batch should return only a small result set.

5. **Reduce stored data**  
   If you’re on n8n Cloud, stop saving successful executions for high-volume workflows [2]. Also avoid manual executions on large runs because they use more memory [6].

6. **Handle retries without redoing everything**  
   n8n doesn’t give a documented checkpoint/restart mechanism in these excerpts. The safe approach is to persist intermediate state yourself between stages, then resume from the last completed stage.

If you tell me whether you’re on **n8n Cloud or self-hosted** and whether you’re already using **queue mode**, I can suggest the exact layout for your case.

You’re describing a classic at-least-once worker queue problem; the safest pattern is to make the claim atomic in PostgreSQL and treat retries as idempotent.

1. Use a single atomic “claim” statement, not a separate `SELECT` then `UPDATE`.
   Your current `UPDATE ... WHERE status='pending' RETURNING *` is already the right shape for atomic claiming in general SQL.

2. For multiple workers, `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` is usually the better dequeue pattern.
   Example pattern:
   ```sql
   WITH cte AS (
     SELECT id
     FROM jobs
     WHERE status = 'pending'
     ORDER BY id
     FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED
     LIMIT 1
   )
   UPDATE jobs j
   SET status = 'processing',
       locked_at = NOW(),
       worker_id = $1,
       updated_at = NOW()
   FROM cte
   WHERE j.id = cte.id
   RETURNING j.*;
   ```
   This prevents two workers from claiming the same row at the same time.

3. Prevent stale/recovered workers from finishing old jobs by adding a lease token.
   Add a `lock_token UUID` column, set it at claim time, and require it on completion:
   ```sql
   UPDATE jobs
   SET status = 'done', updated_at = NOW()
   WHERE id = $job_id
     AND lock_token = $token
     AND status = 'processing';
   ```
   If a worker recovers after the lease expired, its token won’t match, so it can’t overwrite a job another worker has reclaimed.

4. Handle stuck jobs with a lease timeout, not a blind reset.
   Requeue only jobs whose lease expired:
   ```sql
   UPDATE jobs
   SET status = 'pending', worker_id = NULL, lock_token = NULL
   WHERE status = 'processing'
     AND locked_at < NOW() - INTERVAL '5 minutes';
   ```
   Then let the next claim pick them up.

5. Make retries idempotent.
   Even with perfect locking, a crash can happen after side effects but before marking complete. So downstream work should tolerate duplicate delivery.

For n8n specifically, if you’re running multiple workers, that’s queue mode behavior: workers do the actual work, and the main process coordinates it [5][7]. The safe locking strategy itself is standard PostgreSQL practice rather than an n8n-specific setting.

If you want, I can turn your table into a concrete lease-based schema with `lock_token`, claim, heartbeat, timeout, and complete queries.

It uses a separate lock_token column instead of worker_id, which is a valid variant and is explained clearly. It also adds the sound advice to make downstream work idempotent. It has no material errors and nothing unsafe.

The reply directly and accurately answers the customer's question. It provides the exact recommended PostgreSQL pattern matching the reference: atomic dequeue using FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, lease timeout resets, and a token/worker condition to prevent stale workers from overwriting reclaimed jobs.

Your hourly fetch is a classic rate-limit/flaky-upstream case: use the Schedule Trigger to start the run, then add retry handling on the HTTP Request node, and keep the cached result in Redis/Supabase rather than trying to make n8n the frontend cache.

1. **Schedule the run**
   - Use **Schedule Trigger** with a cron expression like `0 * * * *` for “top of the hour” [4].

2. **Retry the API call**
   - Open your **HTTP Request** node.
   - Go to **Settings** and enable **Retry On Fail** [6].
   - Set **Wait Between Tries (ms)** to `30000` for a 30-second retry interval [6].
   - If you want ~5 minutes total, configure the retry count so the total retry window is about 10 attempts.  
   - This is general HTTP retry logic; n8n’s docs specifically describe it for rate-limit style failures [6], and 502/503 flakiness is the same kind of “retry later” pattern.

3. **If you need more control**
   - Build a loop with **Loop Over Items** + **Wait** [1][6].
   - Put **Wait** after the **HTTP Request** node and connect it back to **Loop Over Items** [6].
   - This is better if you want custom logic like “retry only on 502/503, then stop after 5 minutes.”

4. **Store the clean payload externally**
   - For a dashboard, pushing the final JSON to **Redis/Supabase** is the safer design.
   - n8n can serve webhook responses, but webhook response handling has platform limits in queue mode for large payloads [3], so it’s not the best choice as your main cache layer.

5. **Alert on fatal failure**
   - If retries still fail, route the error branch to your Slack/Discord alert node.

If you want, I can sketch the exact node chain for the retry-and-alert pattern.

You’re missing a resumable checkpoint, so a failure forces a restart and can reprocess earlier pages. The n8n-safe pattern is to batch smaller, isolate the work, and make writes idempotent.

1. Replace the `while (true)` Code-node loop with n8n flow control:
   - Use **HTTP Request** for one page at a time.
   - Add **Loop Over Items** and set **Batch Size** to `1` if you want item-by-item processing [5].
   - If you need to process batches, keep the batch size small and add **Wait** between batches to slow retries/rate limits [7].

2. Break the workflow into two parts:
   - Parent workflow: fetch page/batch, then call a child workflow with **Execute Workflow** [2], [4].
   - Child workflow: transform and write to the database.
   - This reduces the amount of data each execution has to hold and makes retries smaller [2], [4].

3. Make the database write idempotent:
   - Use a unique key for each record and **upsert** so reprocessing the same page doesn’t create duplicates.
   - This is general database practice, not n8n-specific.

4. Add your own checkpoint store:
   - Save the last successful `page` or cursor in a DB/table after a successful write.
   - On start, read that value and resume from there.
   - n8n doesn’t provide built-in checkpointing for this pattern in the excerpts you shared; you need to implement it yourself.

5. Avoid large in-memory runs:
   - Large payloads, many nodes, and the **Code** node can increase memory usage [2], [4].
   - If you’re on n8n Cloud, keeping executions small matters because plan memory is limited [2].

If you want, I can sketch a concrete parent/child workflow structure for this pattern using your API page number or cursor.

You’re running into a classic “too much data in memory at once” problem, and the fix is to combine pagination at the API step with batching in n8n, not just slice the already-loaded input.

1. **Paginate the API call**
   - If you use the **HTTP Request** node, handle pagination there so you fetch one page at a time instead of thousands of records at once [6].
   - This is general HTTP/API practice: smaller pages mean less data in memory per execution.

2. **Batch the items in n8n**
   - Add **Loop Over Items** and set **Batch Size** to `1` if you want item-by-item processing, or a larger number like `100` if each item is small [6].
   - n8n docs recommend splitting large datasets into smaller chunks, e.g. process 200 rows at a time instead of 10,000 [1][5].

3. **Do the heavy work in a sub-workflow**
   - Use **Execute Workflow** for the batch processing step [2][5].
   - Keep the sub-workflow returning only a **small result set** to the parent workflow; that’s what actually frees memory between batches [2].

4. **Avoid this pattern**
   - `return $input.all().slice(0, batchSize);`
   - That only trims what one node returns; it does **not** prevent earlier nodes from already holding all records in memory.

5. **If possible, simplify memory-heavy steps**
   - Avoid the **Code** node where you can, and avoid manual executions on large datasets because they use more memory [1][5].

A good default design is: **HTTP Request with pagination → Loop Over Items batch → Execute Workflow for transform/write → return small summary only**.

You’re hitting Facebook’s single-webhook-per-app limitation, not an n8n “2 trigger nodes” limit. [2]

1. Make sure each Meta app is truly separate and each workflow/trigger uses the matching credential for that app. Your setup with 2 apps + 2 credentials is the right direction. [1]
2. Don’t put two Facebook Lead Ads Trigger nodes for the same Meta app in the same workflow if both need to listen at once; Facebook will only keep one registered webhook URL per app. [2]

So the safe pattern is:
- App A → Credential A → Workflow A
- App B → Credential B → Workflow B

If both workflows still don’t receive leads, the most likely issue is on the Meta side: one app’s webhook is replacing the other, or the app is not fully live/authorized yet. [2][3]

296380.text:
What you’re seeing is consistent with queue mode’s distributed execution model: running executions can keep using the workflow data they already picked up, while new executions can start using the updated workflow immediately. Queue mode sends the execution to a worker, and the worker fetches workflow information from the database when it runs [1][2].

1. **Assume in-flight executions are not version-locked to the deploy**  
   n8n’s queue mode is designed so workers execute queued jobs independently [1][5]. That means a deployment can overlap with active runs, so “mixed-version” behavior during a rollout is possible in practice.

2. **Use a rollout strategy that avoids changing workflows mid-flight**  
   The safe production pattern is to **drain/stop workers**, let the queue empty, deploy the new workflow, then bring workers back. This is general distributed-systems practice; n8n docs confirm workers are separate processes and can be scaled up/down independently [1][7].

3. **If you have long-running workflows, avoid editing the live workflow during execution**  
   For long-running jobs, the safest option is to let existing executions finish before publishing changes. If you need concurrent versions, keep separate workflow copies and activate the new one only after the old one is drained. That’s general workflow/versioning practice.

4. **Check the queue-mode prerequisites so behavior is predictable**  
   Make sure all main, worker, and webhook processes share the same `N8N_ENCRYPTION_KEY` and use `EXECUTIONS_MODE=queue` [5]. Also avoid SQLite in queue mode; n8n says distributed queue mode with SQLite isn’t supported/recommended [2][5].

5. **If you’re using webhook processors, treat them the same way in deployments**  
   Webhook processes also rely on Redis and `EXECUTIONS_MODE` [2]. They should be included in the same drain/rollout procedure.

If you want, I can help you turn this into a concrete blue/green or drain-first deployment checklist for your exact setup.

That matches the accepted forum answer. Step 4 (encryption key, SQLite) is tangential padding but harmless, and there is no material error or unsafe advice. The closing offer to build a checklist is mild filler.

The reply accurately identifies why version drift happens across workers in queue mode and provides the correct production strategies: worker draining and workflow versioning. These match the reference packet's accepted solution.

If you want an Airtable replacement for structured data plus automations, the most common production-safe path in n8n is either a real database or n8n Data Tables, depending on how much scale and collaboration you need.

1. For “database + no-code workflows,” use a real database with n8n:
   - Postgres is the most common default choice for production because it’s reliable, expressive, and easier to grow than a spreadsheet-style tool. This is general technical judgment, not n8n-specific.
   - In n8n, connect it with the database node you already use in your stack, and keep the workflow logic in n8n.

2. If you want Airtable-like storage inside n8n itself, consider **Data tables**:
   - n8n documents them as built-in storage for “persisting data across workflows,” “storing markers to prevent duplicate runs,” and “storing evaluation data for AI workflows” [2].
   - You can manage them with the **Data Table node**, the **DataTable API endpoint**, or the **Data tables tab** [2].
   - This is a good fit when the data lives mainly inside n8n and you want to avoid a separate database.

3. If your current pain is Airtable auth, note that n8n supports Airtable with **Personal Access Token (PAT)** or **OAuth2**, and the old API key method is deprecated [6]. Sometimes people “switch” because of that change, not because the workflow design was wrong.

4. If your use case is Airtable-trigger-style polling, n8n’s Airtable Trigger uses polling intervals like Every Minute/Hour/Day/Week/Month or custom cron [8]. If that polling model is part of what you dislike, a database-backed workflow often feels more predictable.

If you want, I can suggest the best fit by use case: “single-user internal ops,” “team collaboration,” or “production app backend.”

310057.text:
You’re trying to prevent an older webhook from overwriting a newer state, which is best handled in PostgreSQL with a monotonic guard.

1. **Add a versioning field to your table**
   Use one of these, in order of preference:
   - `event_version BIGINT` if the source gives a reliable sequence/version
   - `event_timestamp TIMESTAMPTZ` if the source gives a trustworthy event time
   - both, if you want a tie-breaker

2. **Only update when the incoming event is newer**
   General PostgreSQL approach:
   ```sql
   UPDATE orders
   SET
     status = $2,
     event_version = $3,
     updated_at = NOW()
   WHERE id = $1
     AND (event_version IS NULL OR event_version < $3);
   ```
   If you use timestamps:
   ```sql
   UPDATE orders
   SET
     status = $2,
     event_timestamp = $3,
     updated_at = NOW()
   WHERE id = $1
     AND (event_timestamp IS NULL OR event_timestamp < $3);
   ```

3. **Make it atomic**
   Run the check and update in the same SQL statement like above. That avoids a race where two webhook executions read the same old row and both try to write.

4. **If you need retries to be idempotent**
   Keep a separate table of processed event IDs and reject duplicates before updating:
   ```sql
   INSERT INTO processed_events (event_id, order_id)
   VALUES ($1, $2)
   ON CONFLICT (event_id) DO NOTHING;
   ```
   Then only update `orders` if the insert succeeded.

5. **If events can arrive out of order but not all sources are trustworthy**
   Prefer a source-provided sequence/version over your own timestamp. Server receive time is usually not safe for ordering because network delays can reorder arrivals.

If you want, I can turn this into a single `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE` pattern for PostgreSQL that handles both inserts and updates safely.

grades.why: The reply gives the same core fix as the accepted answer: a version column with an atomic UPDATE guarded by a version comparison. It also offers a timestamp variant and an optional dedup table, which are sound general PostgreSQL practice and not harmful. It adds the NULL handling and the point about using source-provided ordering, and it contains no material error.

The reply directly answers the user's question with the correct PostgreSQL pattern: adding a version or timestamp column and checking that incoming values are strictly newer within the WHERE clause of the UPDATE statement. This ensures PostgreSQL evaluates the condition atomically, preventing older out-of-order webhook events from overwriting newer data.

307866.text:
You’re describing a classic at-least-once worker queue problem; the safest pattern is to make the claim atomic in PostgreSQL and treat retries as idempotent.

1. Use a single atomic “claim” statement, not a separate `SELECT` then `UPDATE`.
   Your current `UPDATE ... WHERE status='pending' RETURNING *` is already the right shape for atomic claiming in general SQL.

2. For multiple workers, `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` is usually the better dequeue pattern.
   Example pattern:
   ```sql
   WITH cte AS (
     SELECT id
     FROM jobs
     WHERE status = 'pending'
     ORDER BY id
     FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED
     LIMIT 1
   )
   UPDATE jobs j
   SET status = 'processing',
       locked_at = NOW(),
       worker_id = $1,
       updated_at = NOW()
   FROM cte
   WHERE j.id = cte.id
   RETURNING j.*;
   ```
   This prevents two workers from claiming the same row at the same time.

3. Prevent stale/recovered workers from finishing old jobs by adding a lease token.
   Add a `lock_token UUID` column, set it at claim time, and require it on completion:
   ```sql
   UPDATE jobs
   SET status = 'done', updated_at = NOW()
   WHERE id = $job_id
     AND lock_token = $token
     AND status = 'processing';
   ```
   If a worker recovers after the lease expired, its token won’t match, so it can’t overwrite a job another worker has reclaimed.

4. Handle stuck jobs with a lease timeout, not a blind reset.
   Requeue only jobs whose lease expired:
   ```sql
   UPDATE jobs
   SET status = 'pending', worker_id = NULL, lock_token = NULL
   WHERE status = 'processing'
     AND locked_at < NOW() - INTERVAL '5 minutes';
   ```
   Then let the next claim pick them up.

5. Make retries idempotent.
   Even with perfect locking, a crash can happen after side effects but before marking complete. So downstream work should tolerate duplicate delivery.

For n8n specifically, if you’re running multiple workers, that’s queue mode behavior: workers do the actual work, and the main process coordinates it [5][7]. The safe locking strategy itself is standard PostgreSQL practice rather than an n8n-specific setting.

If you want, I can turn your table into a concrete lease-based schema with `lock_token`, claim, heartbeat, timeout, and complete queries.

It uses a separate lock_token column instead of worker_id, which is a valid variant and is explained clearly. It also adds the sound advice to make downstream work idempotent. It has no material errors and nothing unsafe.

The reply directly and accurately answers the customer's question. It provides the exact recommended PostgreSQL pattern matching the reference: atomic dequeue using FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, lease timeout resets, and a token/worker condition to prevent stale workers from overwriting reclaimed jobs.

You’re missing a resumable checkpoint, so a failure forces a restart and can reprocess earlier pages. The n8n-safe pattern is to batch smaller, isolate the work, and make writes idempotent.

1. Replace the `while (true)` Code-node loop with n8n flow control:
   - Use **HTTP Request** for one page at a time.
   - Add **Loop Over Items** and set **Batch Size** to `1` if you want item-by-item processing [5].
   - If you need to process batches, keep the batch size small and add **Wait** between batches to slow retries/rate limits [7].

2. Break the workflow into two parts:
   - Parent workflow: fetch page/batch, then call a child workflow with **Execute Workflow** [2], [4].
   - Child workflow: transform and write to the database.
   - This reduces the amount of data each execution has to hold and makes retries smaller [2], [4].

3. Make the database write idempotent:
   - Use a unique key for each record and **upsert** so reprocessing the same page doesn’t create duplicates.
   - This is general database practice, not n8n-specific.

4. Add your own checkpoint store:
   - Save the last successful `page` or cursor in a DB/table after a successful write.
   - On start, read that value and resume from there.
   - n8n doesn’t provide built-in checkpointing for this pattern in the excerpts you shared; you need to implement it yourself.

5. Avoid large in-memory runs:
   - Large payloads, many nodes, and the **Code** node can increase memory usage [2], [4].
   - If you’re on n8n Cloud, keeping executions small matters because plan memory is limited [2].

If you want, I can sketch a concrete parent/child workflow structure for this pattern using your API page number or cursor.

270167.text:
You’ve hit a design choice, not a missing Docker setting: in external mode, those Code-node allowlists are meant to be controlled by the launcher config file, not by plain container env vars. [1][2][3]

I can’t confirm the internal rationale beyond the docs, but the safe interpretation is:
1. `NODE_FUNCTION_ALLOW_BUILTIN` / `NODE_FUNCTION_ALLOW_EXTERNAL` for JavaScript, and the Python equivalents, must be set as `env-overrides` in `/etc/n8n-task-runners.json` in external mode. [2][3][4]
2. The runner container’s environment is only used for vars the launcher allowlists via `allowed-env`, while `env-overrides` are explicitly injected by the launcher. [1]
3. n8n’s docs also show the intended pattern: extend the `n8nio/runners` image and copy a custom `n8n-task-runners.json` that contains the allowlists you want. [4]

So yes: if you want different module allowlists, you need to customize `n8n-task-runners.json`; setting only the runner container env vars is not enough in external mode. That’s by design per the documentation, and I can’t verify any “urgent security reason” beyond the general fact that these settings control what Code nodes may import. [2][3]

This is a product-design question rather than a setup bug, so a human from the n8n community/forum would be the right place to ask for the reasoning behind the default config.  

Handoff summary:
- Problem: external task runners ignore Code-node allowlist env vars unless they’re set as launcher `env-overrides` in `n8n-task-runners.json`.
- Setup: n8n 2.10.1, Docker on Ubuntu 24.04, external task-runners container.

grades.why: The reply correctly explains that env-overrides take precedence over container env vars and that the fix is to supply a custom n8n-task-runners.json, which matches the reference's key step. It points to extending the image rather than mounting the file, but both are documented and valid. It also honestly says it can't confirm the design rationale and sends the customer to the forum for that, so it counts as mixed. It does not mention the open feature request, which is a minor omission.
